name: Season Parks
lines: Midwinter, and it stays midwinter here
The Great Yule Tree
The Hot Chocolate Hut
thick and sweet, with cream on top
You wrap both hands round a cup of hot chocolate. It is far too hot, and perfect.
hot from the brazier
A paper cone of chestnuts, split and steaming. You burn your fingers on the first one, as everybody does.
The Gingerbread Stall
houses, stars and little men
A gingerbread star, iced in white, with your initial on it.
Candles and Lanterns
light for the longest night
A beeswax candle for the window, to light somebody home.
scarves, mittens, hats with bobbles
A striped scarf, long enough to go round three times.
Toys and Ornaments
glass baubles and wooden toys
A glass bauble with a snowy village painted inside it.
Snow on every path, and it never melts.
The Great Yule Tree is lit all night, every night.
Skate the Frozen Lake: the ice will hold.
The eggs are painted and the fire is lit
daffodils, tulips, lilac
A bunch of daffodils, wrapped in paper, still wet from the bucket.
Lemonade and Hot Cross Buns
fresh this morning
A glass of cloudy lemonade and a hot cross bun, split and buttered.
The blossom is always out here.
Dance round the Great Maypole: twelve ribbons, twelve colours.
Sit by the Duck Pond and watch the ducks.
The longest day, held
The Sunflower Field
The Ice Cream Cart
vanilla, strawberry, chocolate
A cone with two scoops, already melting down your wrist.
The Lemonade Stand
Lemonade so cold it hurts your teeth, with a slice of lemon floating in it.
Long grass, long light, and the band plays in the evening.
Take a swan boat round the Fountain Lake.
Get lost in the sunflowers: they are taller than you.
The harvest in, and the dead remembered
pressed here, this morning
A cup of warm spiced cider and a crisp red apple for the way home.
pumpkin, apple, blackberry
A slice of pumpkin pie, still warm, with a dollop of cream.
The leaves fall all year here, and never run out.
Find the middle of the Hay Maze and ring the bell.
Pick a pumpkin from the patch (they grow back by morning).
🎄 The Great Yule Tree · press E
🎄 The Great Yule Tree
Seventeen metres of fir, lit every night
The tree is dressed with
glass baubles and a spiral of
warm lights, and a star at the very top.
Bringing an evergreen indoors at midwinter is an old custom across northern Europe: proof that something stays green and alive in the dark of the year.
The presents round its foot are for looking at. Everybody tries to guess what is in the tall one.
🎀 The Great Maypole · press E to dance round it
🎀 Round the Great Maypole and back. The ribbons are plaited a little tighter for your dance.
🎺 The Bandstand · press E to see what the band is playing
🍂 The Harvest Feast · press E to sit down
🍂 The Harvest Feast
A long table, always laid
Bread from the first and last of the corn, apples, nuts, squashes from the patch and a jug of cider: the harvest in.
At the far end a place is always laid for whoever is missing this year. Nobody sits there; everybody raises a cup to it.
Under the lanterns after dark the table is the warmest place in the city.
⛸️ The Frozen Lake · press E to skate a lap
⛸️ A whole lap of the Frozen Lake without falling over. Nearly.
🦆 The Duck Pond · press E to call the ducks over
🦆 The ducks turn round and come paddling over to see what you have. (Nothing, as it turns out. They forgive you.)
🦢 The Fountain Lake · press E to take a swan boat round
🦢 Once round the Fountain Lake by swan boat, past the fountain twice. You are only slightly damp.
🌷 The Tulip Gardens · press E
🌷 The Tulip Gardens
Eight beds, eight colours,
Tulips came to Europe from the Ottoman gardens in the 1500s; in the Dutch 'tulip mania' of the 1630s a single bulb could sell for more than a house.
Walk between the beds along the gravel. Please do not pick them: the gardeners count.
🌻 The Sunflower Field · press E
🌻 The Sunflower Field
sunflowers, all taller than you
Young sunflowers turn to follow the sun across the sky; grown ones settle facing east.
Walk the path through the middle, or step in among them and see how quickly you lose your way.
🎃 The Pumpkin Patch · press E to pick a pumpkin
🔔 The middle of the Hay Maze! · press E to ring the bell
🌾 The Hay Maze · press E
Seven by seven, two bales high
Find your way to the bell in the middle and ring it. The maze times you from the moment you step in.
It is the same maze for everybody, so you can race your friends.
You stop and step off.
metres, inside the railings
Your best in the maze
are hidden round the park every day: walk up to one and press E to pick it up.
The gates: the main gate on the far temple street, a side gate either side of it, and a gate at each end.

Under the Double Eagle
The Summer Garden's band
The band plays the old marches and rags of the bandstand's heyday, a new piece every ten minutes.
Step up onto the bandstand and stand with them, or take a bench and listen.
🎃 You have already picked your pumpkin today. They grow back by morning.
a round orange one
a tall knobbly one
a pale white ghost pumpkin
a little striped gourd
a great heavy one you can barely lift
from the Pumpkin Patch.
